# Parley v0.1.37

One fix: a question sent with Ask could, in a particular sequence, be answered
with the wrong answer and report success.

## A question now carries its own id

When Parley delivers a question, it tells the receiving agent how to reply. It
used to say "run `parley answer current`", and explicitly told the agent not to
copy the question's id. `current` means "the question this pane is currently
holding" — which is not necessarily the question the agent was working on.

That matters in one sequence, and it is not exotic:

1. You ask an agent a question. It is busy, and the question eventually times
   out. Your pane stops waiting.
2. Someone asks that same agent a different question.
3. The first agent finishes the original work and replies with `answer current`.
4. The reply lands on the **second** question.

The second asker receives an answer to a question it never asked, and Parley
reports it as a normal successful answer. Nothing anywhere reports a problem.

Delivered questions now name their own id and say to use it exactly. The id
identifies one specific question, so a late reply can only ever go to the
question it was written for.

This aligns delivery with the agent protocol, which already said to reply using
the exact command the question supplies. The instructions Parley generated were
contradicting it.

`parley answer current` still works for a pane holding a single question and
remains part of the protocol. What changed is that questions no longer teach it.

## A reply to a closed question now explains itself

If an agent replies to a question that has already timed out, been cancelled or
been answered, it used to receive "unknown consultation" — which reads like a
fault in Parley and invites the agent to try again, which can never work.

It now reports which state the question reached and when, and that the reply was
not delivered. Only the agent that was actually asked is told anything; any
other pane still receives the bare refusal.

## Not fixed

An agent can still type `parley answer current` from habit, or from an older
question still visible in its scrollback. This removes the instruction that
taught it. It cannot prevent it.

## On Ask blocking the sending pane

This work started from a different question: whether `parley ask` could stop
blocking the pane that sends it. The short answer is that it cannot, without
either duplicating what Delegate already does or rebuilding how deadlines are
owned — and the obvious cheap version, shortening the Ask timeout, makes things
worse rather than better, because the timeout is measured from when the question
was sent. Shortening it would reject more answers that were genuinely on their
way.

For work that may take a while, or when the other agent may be busy, Delegate
remains the right tool: it does not block, it is tracked, and its result comes
back properly. The full reasoning, including where the two reviewing agents
disagreed, is in `docs/ask-caller-bound-proposal.md`.

## Compatibility

Agent protocol is unchanged at 32, so **no pane needs restarting**. The reply
instructions are written fresh for each question, so panes already running pick
up the new form on their next question.

Validated: 338 native checks, 53 Node tests, public scan, platform scan and
build. The two substantive checks were watched failing before the fix was made.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
